samples.summary: Renderer guard for legacy `color: ''` is missing in the table text path, so the issue's symptom persists for text inside tables
samples.evidence:
The task doc promises "Renderer treats a falsy resolved color as unset, so documents already saved with `color: ""` … render with the theme default instead of a stale `fillStyle`" and enumerates paintRun / renderListMarker / resolveColorAtPosition. But table cell text is painted by a separate path that still uses `??`:
packages/docs/src/view/table-renderer.ts:457 `const runTextColor = defaultColorResolver(style.color) ?? Theme.defaultColor;`
packages/docs/src/view/table-renderer.ts:564 `ctx.fillStyle = defaultColorResolver(cellBlock.inlines[0]?.style.color) ?? Theme.defaultColor;`
With a stored empty string these assign `''`, which the canvas ignores — exactly the failure mode of #728 (the previous pass is the selection/backgrounds fill). Acceptance criterion "reset the text color → the text is uncolored" therefore still fails for already-saved docs whose colored text lives in a table.

samples.summary: Falsy-color normalization is scattered across consumers instead of done once in `defaultColorResolver` / the color model
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:75,80 and packages/docs/src/view/paint-layout.ts:389,558 each switch `??`→`||` at the call site, with a three-line comment repeated at each site. Normalizing `''` → `undefined` inside `defaultColorResolver` (the single resolver every consumer already routes through, per model/color.ts) would cover every present and future consumer — including table-renderer and the underline-color site — with one change and no per-site invariant to remember. Approach preference, not a blocker.

samples.summary: `style.underlineColor` still falls back with `??`, leaving one same-shaped color path unguarded in the file the fix touched
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/paint-layout.ts:454 `ctx.strokeStyle = resolveColor(style.underlineColor) ?? textColor;` — an empty-string underlineColor would silently keep the previous strokeStyle, the identical hazard the diff documents two dozen lines above. No UI currently resets underlineColor (grep found no frontend writer), so this is defensive consistency rather than a live bug; the issue's Non-goals do not exclude it.

samples.summary: Sheets toolbar keeps the empty-string reset convention, leaving the repo with two contradictory "clear a color" idioms
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/components/formatting-toolbar.tsx:200 `spreadsheet?.applyStyle({ tc: "" })` and :213 `{ bg: "" }` still write `""` to clear. The change under review declares in two places that "`undefined` — not `""` — clears the color" (text-format-group.tsx:124-126, docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:402-404). The issue's Non-goals scope the fix to docs, and sheets' style model may legitimately treat `""` as a clear, so this is not an acceptance gap — but the newly-stated invariant now has an unannotated exception a future reader will trip over.

finding.summary: Renderer guard for legacy `color: ''` is missing in the table text path, so the issue's symptom persists for text inside tables
finding.evidence:
The task doc promises "Renderer treats a falsy resolved color as unset, so documents already saved with `color: ""` … render with the theme default instead of a stale `fillStyle`" and enumerates paintRun / renderListMarker / resolveColorAtPosition. But table cell text is painted by a separate path that still uses `??`:
packages/docs/src/view/table-renderer.ts:457 `const runTextColor = defaultColorResolver(style.color) ?? Theme.defaultColor;`
packages/docs/src/view/table-renderer.ts:564 `ctx.fillStyle = defaultColorResolver(cellBlock.inlines[0]?.style.color) ?? Theme.defaultColor;`
With a stored empty string these assign `''`, which the canvas ignores — exactly the failure mode of #728 (the previous pass is the selection/backgrounds fill). Acceptance criterion "reset the text color → the text is uncolored" therefore still fails for already-saved docs whose colored text lives in a table.

verdict.reason: The quoted evidence is accurate. table-renderer.ts:457 and :564 still use `??` against `defaultColorResolver`, which passes a stored empty-string color through verbatim (model/color.ts:14-22), so `ctx.fillStyle = ''` is ignored by the canvas and the prior fillStyle (selection fill at table-renderer.ts:442, or a preceding colored run at :458) persists. Table cell text is a genuinely separate painter from the fixed `paintRun` path — doc-canvas imports renderTableBackgrounds/renderTableContent rather than renderTable (asserted in test/view/table-renderer.test.ts:533-539) — and paint-layout.ts:389 shows the intended guard form (`|| undefined`) is applied only on the body path, with resolveColorAtPosition guarded via `||` at color.ts:75,80. I searched for an upstream normalization that would make the table guard unnecessary and found none: yorkie-doc-store.ts:121 serializes `''` and :176 reads it back unchanged, and the task doc Non-goals (lines 51-52) explicitly forgo a migration because "the renderer guard makes already-stored empty values render correctly". The guard therefore does not cover table text, so the acceptance criterion "reset the text color → the text is uncolored" still fails for already-saved documents whose colored text lives in a table — an unmet acceptance criterion, major under this lens.
